quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road where you can see traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the road for a long time without looking around.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep before driving.
Driving short distances on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for a long time without looking around.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and stop checking around you. You may zone out and miss traffic slowing or stopping ahead.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot see all areas. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: When should you stop for a school bus with red flashing lights?

options.text: Until all students get off the bus.
Until the stop arm goes back in.
Until the stop arm goes back in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Until the stop arm goes back in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm retracts, and the bus starts moving again.

questions.question: What should you do if you are driving in another driver's blind spot?

options.text: Move forward or back so the driver can see you.
Keep the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in someone's blind spot. Move ahead or drop back so they can see you.

questions.question: Why do large trucks need extra space in front of them?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck can stop safely.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck can stop safely.
questions.explanation: Trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Falling rocks
Trucks use second gear
Steep hill ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells you a steep hill is ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A lane is ending.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers that a lane is ending. Be ready to merge safely with other traffic.

questions.question: What does this warning sign tell drivers?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming.
There is road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane on a multi-lane road ends ahead. Drivers in that lane must move to the left.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A sharp right turn ahead.
Another road joins from the right.
The road turns sharp right, then sharp left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharp right, then sharp left.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells you the road will turn sharply right and then sharply left ahead.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spots when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When you approach a stop sign without a crosswalk, you must stop your vehicle before entering the intersection.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign. Stop at the stop line if there is one. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. You should:

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake immediately after a blowout. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the accelerator. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull to a safe area.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all your windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, return to your original lane when:

options.text: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough room to safely pull in front of that vehicle.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than you would on a city street:

options.text: To spot potential hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.
Because it helps you keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot potential hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, be ready for changes in traffic. Watch for signals from other drivers. Expect vehicles merging at on-ramps and be prepared for rapid changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured away from the scene immediately.
Always leave the injured where they are.
Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless necessary. Moving them without training can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until medical help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not stop when entering the interstate. Use the acceleration lane to speed up and smoothly merge with the fast-moving traffic already on the highway.

questions.question: You see a red traffic light, but a police officer directs you to go through the intersection without stopping. You should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: A bicyclist who does not obey traffic laws:

options.text: Does not have to obey traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
Will have their bicycle impounded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, what should drivers do?

options.text: Stop inside the roundabout.
Yield to cars entering the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection. Cars flow counterclockwise around a center island. There are no traffic signals. When entering, you must yield to cars already in the roundabout. Then follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means do not cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you may cross to pass, but only if it is safe and you will not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This is true even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: Which describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They trust that other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect bad driving and do not show courtesy.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting possible mistakes from other drivers and being ready to handle them.

questions.question: How many drinks does it take to affect your driving?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will move to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: If you are entering from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers on the public road. Merge safely when you have a clear opportunity.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus picking up or dropping off children, come to a complete stop before reaching the bus. This applies no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you may stop only:

options.text: Long enough to unload packages.
To avoid a problem with other traffic.
To let passengers out.
For less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid a problem with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a conflict with another vehicle.

questions.question: Where can drivers make a U-turn?

options.text: On a freeway
Near the top of a hill
In the middle of a curve
Where it will not disrupt traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Where it will not disrupt traffic
questions.explanation: A U-turn is a 180-degree turn that reverses your direction. You may only make a U-turn if you can do it safely and without disrupting other traffic.
